alerts.title: NH-44 shut again at Dewal-Samroli (Udhampur) after fresh mudslides, shooting stones
alerts.summary: The Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) has been repeatedly closed through early August at the Dewal-Samroli stretch (Km 79) in Udhampur district, with fresh mudslides, shooting stones and slushy conditions forcing traffic suspension even after earlier restoration. The Centre has since listed damage across five separate J&K NH stretches this season.
alerts.impact: Kashmir Valley linehaul remains the single point of failure via NH44 — Srinagar, Baramulla, Anantnag, Budgam hubs face repeat multi-day TAT breaches each time this stretch shuts. Keep buffer stock pre-positioned at Jammu, hold NS flags ready for Valley pincodes, and treat this corridor as a standing non-adherence root cause through August.

alerts.title: Jammu-Rajouri National Highway blocked by landslide; PWD restoration hampered by fresh slides
alerts.summary: A landslide blocked the Jammu-Rajouri National Highway, stranding vehicles on both sides. Continuous rainfall has caused extensive damage to roads and public infrastructure across Rajouri district, and PWD's JCB-led restoration work is being repeatedly undone by fresh landslides during active rain spells.
alerts.impact: Rajouri/Poonch-bound LM routes at risk of repeat closures — pre-clear non-serviceable flags for affected talukas and route Rajouri-bound parcels via alternate approach roads where 3P partners have coverage until PWD confirms a stable reopening.

alerts.title: 185 roads shut across Himachal — 92 in Mandi, 48 in Kullu, 14 in Shimla — after torrential rain
alerts.summary: Torrential rain has closed 185 roads across Himachal Pradesh as of Aug 8, concentrated in Mandi (92), Kullu (48) and Shimla (14) districts, alongside 77 disrupted water schemes and 104 damaged transformers. IMD has issued an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rain through Aug 10, and 65 people have died in rain-related incidents since the monsoon began.
alerts.impact: Mandi and Kullu hub LM routes carry the heaviest hit — flag rural pincodes in these two districts for temporary NS status, hold buffer stock at Shimla/Mandi hubs, and expect non-adherence to stay elevated at least through Aug 10 per IMD's own timeline.

alerts.title: Recurring landslides cut NH-37 near Rongdai, Nungba Bazar & Luangchum villages in Noney district
alerts.summary: Days of incessant rain have triggered repeated landslides along the Imphal-Jiribam National Highway (NH-37) in Manipur's Noney district — at Rongdai (2 km from Nungba Bazar), near Nungba Merryland, and between Luangchum and Awangkhul Part-I/Part-II villages — each freshly blocking stretches NHIDCL clears days earlier. Over 100 goods-laden trucks have been stranded near the CPFP camp at Nungba at various points.
alerts.impact: This is Manipur's lifeline for FM inbound goods — treat Noney district as a standing bottleneck through August. Pre-build 5-7 day buffer stock for Imphal hub, expect essential-commodity delays, and coordinate with 3P partners on single-lane convoy timing once NHIDCL reopens a lane.

alerts.title: NH-2 shut daily 6am-6pm at Phesama sinking zone (Kohima-Mao) as hill slope keeps sliding
alerts.summary: The Kohima district administration has ordered repeated daytime closures of NH-2 at the Phesama sinking zone (Km 191+840 to 192+100) on the Kohima-Mao corridor, most recently through Aug 4, to allow NHIDCL to carry out slope-stabilisation work amid continued boulder-fall risk. Light vehicles are diverted via Phesama-Kisama-Kigwema; heavy vehicles bound for Manipur are routed via Peren district.
alerts.impact: Kohima-Mao FM linehaul into Manipur loses its daytime window on this stretch — schedule Manipur-bound dispatches for early morning or evening outside the 6am-6pm closure, or route HMVs via Peren as NHIDCL advises, to avoid TAT breaches on this specific 260m stretch.

alerts.title: Assam floods: toll at 87, 1.3 lakh people still affected across 335 villages in five districts
alerts.summary: Assam's flood death toll has risen to 87, with roughly 1.3 lakh people still affected across 335 villages in Golaghat, Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo and Dhemaji districts. Cloudbursts in upstream tributaries like the Dikhow and Dhansiri caused sudden surges ahead of the Brahmaputra's own peak, flooding areas that rarely see water, with 15,422 hectares of farmland submerged. IMD has forecast further extremely heavy rain in neighbouring Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya that could feed back into these districts.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss risk concentrated in Golaghat, Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo, Dhemaji pincodes — maintain NS flags for the worst-hit revenue circles and route Guwahati hub outbound around the flooded belt; watch for a second surge if Arunachal/Meghalaya rain feeds back into these five districts this week.

alerts.title: Brahmaputra erosion swallows land in Dibrugarh's Chabua-Pukhurijan belt & Barkhetri's Doulashal
alerts.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma inspected erosion-hit villages in Dibrugarh district — Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria — announcing an IIT-Guwahati-led study and a proposed Rs 90 crore mitigation project. Separately, residents of Doulashal village in Barkhetri report nearly a month of relentless Brahmaputra erosion advancing dangerously close to the embankment near Roumari Pathar.
alerts.impact: Early-warning signal, not yet a full stoppage: flag Dibrugarh and Barkhetri-area delivery points for road-access risk if erosion reaches approach roads or the embankment; no NS flags needed yet but worth a monthly recheck given the pace reported by residents.

alerts.title: Kerala orange alert in 9 districts incl. Idukki, Wayanad, Kannur; schools shut, extremely heavy rain isolated spots
alerts.summary: IMD has kept Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod on orange alert, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall (>20cm/24h) flagged for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam and Idukki. Educational institutions have been shut in several districts, and squally coastal weather has kept fishermen off the Kerala-Karnataka-Lakshadweep coast. Rain is forecast to continue through Aug 10.
alerts.impact: Idukki, Wayanad and Kannur hill-taluka LM routes are the most exposed — pre-empt SLA relaxation for these pincodes through Aug 10, and watch Kochi hub inbound linehaul for delays from waterlogging in Ernakulam/Alappuzha.

alerts.title: Saurashtra flooding: red alert for Morbi, Surendranagar, Rajkot, Ahmedabad; 4 dead, evacuations underway
alerts.summary: IMD issued a red alert for heavy to very heavy rain across six Gujarat districts including Morbi, Surendranagar, Rajkot and Ahmedabad as the rain spell shifted into Saurashtra, causing widespread waterlogging; four deaths were reported and severely flooded areas evacuated. Gujarat's CM has held emergency review meetings on the flood situation.
alerts.impact: Rajkot and Morbi hub LM routes at risk of waterlogging-driven delays — hold buffer stock at Ahmedabad and monitor Surendranagar rural pincodes for temporary NS flags if waterlogging persists beyond this week.

alerts.title: Orange alert for Raigad district & Pune Ghats as Konkan braces for another heavy-rain spell
alerts.summary: IMD has issued a fresh orange alert for Raigad district and the Pune Ghat region, forecasting isolated heavy to very heavy rain over the following 24-48 hours, with the wider heavy-rain band concentrated over Konkan, the Ghats and eastern Vidarbha. Raigad remains India's most landslide-scarred district from past monsoons (Irshalwadi, 2023), keeping authorities on alert for slope failures.
alerts.impact: Mumbai-Pune-JNPA linehaul and Raigad rural LM routes should carry extra transit buffer through this spell — pre-flag ghat-adjacent Raigad talukas for possible short-notice NS status if slope warnings escalate.

alerts.title: IMD squally-weather advisory for Bay of Bengal off WB-Odisha-north AP coast & Andaman Sea through Aug 12
alerts.summary: IMD has issued squally weather warnings (strong winds, rough seas) along and off the West Bengal, Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh coasts through Aug 9, over the Andaman Sea through Aug 12, and off the south Sri Lanka coast/south Bay of Bengal through Aug 9, advising fishermen not to venture out. No cyclonic system has organised yet; the Bay of Bengal remains at the start of its post-monsoon storm-formation window.
alerts.impact: No LM/FM action needed yet — early watch only. Track for potential port-side FM disruption at Kolkata/Paradip/Visakhapatnam if the system organises further; no current impact on inland routing.

alerts.title: Petrol/diesel hold steady at multi-city highs; Bengaluru & Hyderabad petrol above ₹111-115/litre
alerts.summary: Retail petrol and diesel prices remain steady but elevated as of Aug 9: Delhi ₹102.12/₹95.20 (petrol/diesel), Mumbai ₹111.21/₹97.83, Bengaluru ₹111.68/₹98.80, Hyderabad ₹115.43/₹103.82, Chennai ₹107.76/₹99.55. No fluctuation over the past week; LPG/CNG/PNG also unchanged.
alerts.impact: Cost watch, no action yet: sustained high fuel levels keep pressure on 3P per-km rates in southern metros especially. Track weekly for early signal on Delhivery/Shadowfax/Xpressbees fuel-surcharge asks ahead of the next OMC pricing cycle.
